cards.text: It's the days of Josiah, king of Judah, the southern kingdom, and the LORD speaks to Jeremiah, His prophet. Israel, the northern kingdom, was carried away to Assyria years before (2 Kings 17:6). Now God says faithless Israel has gone up on every high hill and under every green tree to prostitute herself there.

cards.question: Israel has been chasing other gods on every high hill. After all that, what did God think she would do?

cards.text: But she did not return. And her unfaithful sister Judah saw the whole thing from the front row.

cards.question: Because faithless Israel committed adultery, what did God give her before sending her away?
Judah watched Israel get sent away, and it scared Judah into staying faithful.

cards.text: Judah had no fear and did the same thing. Israel had committed adultery with stones and trees, and friend, I lived in a junk drawer with dead batteries for years without ONCE asking one for a blessing.

cards.question: In spite of all this, Judah came back to God not with all her heart, but only in ___.

cards.text: Pretense. Judah showed up the way some of us show up to a work meeting: camera off, mic muted, already back in bed.

cards.question: The LORD tells Jeremiah that faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than unfaithful Judah.

cards.text: WAIT. The one who got sent away with divorce papers comes out looking BETTER? Then God sends Jeremiah to call toward the north, and the message starts with "Return, O faithless Israel," and keeps going.

cards.question: God says He will no longer look on Israel with anger, because He is ___.
God says His anger won't last forever. What's the one thing He asks Israel to do?

cards.text: That's it, friend: no forms in triplicate, no waiting room, just own what you did. Then God calls again, "Return, O faithless children," and says He is their master.

cards.question: God says He'll take them, one from a city and two from a family, and bring them to ___.
God promises to give them shepherds after His own heart. What will those shepherds feed them with?

cards.text: Then God looks ahead to "those days," when they multiply and increase in the land. And He brings up the ark of the covenant.

cards.question: In those days, God says the ark of the covenant will never even come to mind.
At that time, all the nations will be gathered in Jerusalem to honor the name of the LORD. What will they call Jerusalem?
At that time, God says they will no longer follow the stubbornness of their evil hearts.
In those days, the house of Judah will walk with the house of ___, coming together from the land of the north.

cards.text: Then God says what He longed for: "How I long to make you My sons and give you a desirable land, the most beautiful inheritance of all the nations!"

cards.question: God says He thought they would call Him ___ and never turn away from following Him.

cards.text: But that's not how it went. "But as a woman may betray her husband, so you have betrayed Me, O house of Israel," declares the LORD.
Then a voice is heard on the barren heights. It's the children of Israel, weeping and begging for mercy.

cards.question: Why are the children of Israel weeping and begging for mercy on the barren heights?

answers.text: They had turned away and forgotten the LORD
Enemies had taken away all their land
Their king had been killed in battle

cards.question: Then God calls out, "Return, O faithless children," and makes a promise. What does He promise to do about their faithlessness?

cards.text: And THIS time, they answer: "Here we are. We come to You, for You are the LORD our God." Friend, that's the sound of somebody finally picking up after the phone rang all day.

cards.question: The people say their salvation comes from the hills and the mountains.

cards.text: Then they admit what that shameful god has cost them. From their youth, it has consumed what their fathers worked for: flocks, herds, even their sons and daughters.

cards.question: With all that out in the open, who do the people say has sinned against the LORD their God?
The people confess that from their youth even to this day, they have not obeyed the voice of the LORD.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks, and it starts with an if: "If you will return, O Israel, return to Me," declares the LORD.

cards.question: If Israel will return, what does God say they need to remove from His sight?
If they swear by the LORD in truth, in justice and in righteousness, then the ___ will be blessed by Him.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells the men of Judah and Jerusalem, "Break up your unplowed ground, and do not sow among the thorns." It's like dough that sat out all night: NOTHING gets stamped into it until you work it first.

cards.question: God tells the men of Judah to circumcise themselves to the LORD. What does He tell them to remove the foreskins of?
God warns Judah that if they don't change, His wrath will flare up for a moment and then pass.

cards.text: A fire no one can put out, because of their evil deeds. Heavy words to end on, friend, but listen to the one word this passage keeps calling out: return.

findings.problem: The card states two facts from outside the passage with no reference. Jeremiah 3:6 says only "King Josiah," but the card calls him "king of Judah" and calls Judah "the southern kingdom." The Assyria fact on the same card has its reference (2 Kings 17:6), but these facts don't. Josiah as king of Judah could cite Jeremiah 1:2.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card is only a setup phrase and a Bible quote. Papa Dorin's voice is missing, so it reads like a verse on a screen and not a storyteller.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This is the passage's big betrayal moment (Jeremiah 3:20), but the card is just "But that's not how it went" plus the verse quoted word for word. It has no reaction and none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. "Their detestable idols" has the Bible's adjective "detestable," and the wrong answers ("Their foreign wives" and "Their city walls") have no adjective like it. The right answer sounds more like the Bible than the others.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Jeremiah 4:4 says God's wrath "will break out like fire and burn with no one to extinguish it." The card says "A fire no one can put out," which drops the "like" and turns the comparison into a plain fact.
